Tone-adjusted summary: The FOMC statement is broadly supportive—economic activity and employment are strengthening, financial conditions remain accommodative, and policy is highly supportive (ZLB, ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases). Inflation is described as largely transitory, and the Fed reiterates its commitment to average 2 percent inflation and maximum employment.

SLOOS lens: The latest Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to improving credit supply that broadly corroborates the accommodative financial conditions cited by the Fed.
- Directionally, banks eased standards across several household segments (residential real estate, credit cards, auto, and other consumer loans), and reduced minimum required credit scores, signaling normalization and better access to credit for households.
- Large banks also eased standards on HELOCs, GSE-eligible mortgages, and for investment-grade firms, implying easier financing for higher-quality borrowers.
- However, relative to pre-pandemic levels, some banks still report tighter standards in consumer categories, and foreign banks tightened standards for below-investment-grade firms; some large banks also tightened certain C&I loan policies. This indicates lingering constraints for riskier borrowers even as overall conditions improve.

FSR lens: Financial stability vulnerabilities (elevated valuations, high business leverage, sensitivity to rapid shifts in conditions) continue to temper the outlook.

Net: The SLOOS evidence of broad easing in household credit and for IG corporates modestly improves the outlook for credit availability versus the prior assessment, while lingering tightness for riskier borrowers and FSR-flagged vulnerabilities keep the tone from being overly buoyant.
